subject: Modeling flight altitudes with a latent parameter

messages.author: 93877f147a1367c1
messages.subject: Modeling flight altitudes with a latent parameter
parts:
Posting for a colleague - 


Hi folks,
I have a model that's trying to fit a gamma distribution to bird altitudes during migration, recorded via GPS transmitters. Our data consists of ~13,000 altitude measurements that are recorded during the day and/or outside of migratory time periods, and so can be safely assumed to be ground locations (true altitude of 0 m). We have another ~ 430 altitude measurements that could potentially be flight locations based on the date and time when they are recorded, but their true movement state is uncertain. Designating this movement state is difficult due to the substantial measurement error in the altitudes (+/- 50 m) and the small number of true flight locations in the sample (believed to be ~33% of recorded nocturnal locations from a prior analysis).

I've built a JAGS model that can infer the measurement error, true movement states, and the distribution of flight locations from the data. In short, it uses the known ground locations to infer the altitudinal measurement error, and then infers unknown states based on the likelihood that a given altitude is solely a result of that measurement error. The measurement error parameters both converge to R-hat values < 1.1 quickly, but the shape and rate parameters take an abnormally large number of iterations (at least 200k) to converge.

After some time working with the simulation, I'm pretty sure that the small sample size of flight locations, combined with the latent variable, are the reasons that the model is taking so long to converge. The model also really doesn't seem to like the gamma distribution; the simulation works much better with a normal distribution, but unfortunately a normal distribution isn't a great fit for the real data. 

My questions are:
1) Is the high number of iterations required for convergence a red flag that I shouldn't trust the model output?
2) Is there a way to reparameterize the model so that it samples more effectively? I'm particularly curious about the gamma distribution here. I've also considered moving over to Stan, as it seems to have better mechanisms for dealing with discrete latent variables (i.e. marginalizing them out) but I wanted to rule out a potential JAGS solution first.

I've included a simulation using the model below; note that altitude values (referenced as height above terrain, or HAT, in the code) are scaled with 0 as ground height and 1 being the maximum possible altitude.

Thanks for your time,
Liam Berigan

library(tidyverse)
library(jagsUI)
library(here)

known_ground <- 13000
unknown_flight <- 150
unknown_ground <- 280

# unknown_flight <- 150*50 #model converges with more samples
# unknown_ground <- 280*50

shape <- 1.2470108
rate <- 7.8222304
mean <- shape/rate
sd <- (shape/(rate^2))^.5

measurement_error <- 50/2183.475 #standardized by maximum altitude

known_ground_df <- tibble(HAT = rnorm(n=known_ground, mean=0, sd=measurement_error), HAT_index = rep(1, known_ground))
unknown_ground_df <- tibble(HAT = rnorm(n=unknown_ground, mean=0, sd=measurement_error), HAT_index = rep(NA, unknown_ground))

unknown_flight_df <- tibble(HAT = rgamma(unknown_flight, shape = shape, rate = rate), HAT_index = rep(NA, unknown_flight))
unknown_flight_df$HAT <- map(unknown_flight_df$HAT, function(x){
  rnorm(n=1, mean = x, sd=measurement_error)
}) %>%
  unlist()

dt <- bind_rows(known_ground_df, unknown_ground_df, unknown_flight_df)

sink(here("simulation_gamma.jags"))
cat("model{
   # likelihood
    for (i in 1:n_obs){
    HAT[i] ~ dnorm(mu_observed[i], tau_error) # adding gps-specific error
    mu_observed[i] <- mu_bias + (HAT_index[i]-1)*real_alt[i] # on average, the observed altitude should be the real altitude + the average bias
    real_alt[i] ~ dgamma(shape_flight, rate_flight) # distribution of real flight altitudes
    }
   
    #priors
    for (k in 1:n_obs){
    HAT_index[k] ~ dcat(c(0.67, 0.33)) # 1 is a ground location, 2 is a flight location.
    }
   
    mu_bias ~ dnorm(0, 1) #negative values allowed
    tau_error <- pow(sigma_error, -2) #precision
    sigma_error ~ dnorm(0, 1) T(0,) #standard deviation
   
    shape_flight ~ dnorm(0, prec_shape) T(0,)
    prec_shape <- pow(5, -2)
    rate_flight ~ dnorm(0, prec_rate) T(0,)
    prec_rate <- pow(10, -2)

}  
    ")
sink()

inits <- function(){list(mu_bias = rnorm(1,0,1),
                         sigma_error = runif(1,0,1),
                         shape_flight = runif(1,0,5), #
                         rate_flight = runif(1,0,10))}

parameters <- c("mu_bias", "sigma_error", "shape_flight", "rate_flight") #

jags_data <- list(HAT = dt$HAT,
                  n_obs = nrow(dt),
                  HAT_index = dt$HAT_index)
# running jags
nc <- 3 # number of chains
ni <- 5000 # number of iterations
nb <- 2000 # burnin
nt <- 1 # thin rate (keeps every 5th iteration)
m_test <- jags(data=jags_data, inits=inits, parameters.to.save = parameters,
               model.file=here("simulation_gamma.jags"), n.chains=nc, n.iter=ni, n.burnin=nb,
               parallel=T)

print(m_test)

traceplot(m_test)
